summary: The Iran Human Rights, Internet Freedom, and Accountability Act of 2026 establishes policies and programs to support human rights, expand unrestricted internet access, and hold the regime of the Islamic Republic of Iran accountable for internal repression and corruption. The bill requires federal updates on internet freedom strategies, extends authorizations for internet freedom grants, directs the Defense Innovation Unit to develop anti-censorship technologies, mandates reports on Iranian political figures and parastatal entities, establishes an Iran Kleptocracy Initiative within FinCEN to target illicit assets, creates a congressional nomination process for human rights sanctions, and outlines a sense of Congress regarding broadcasting and support for independent journalists.

affected_groups.effect: Aims to expand unrestricted internet access, communication lines, independent journalism, and potentially repurpose seized illicit assets for their benefit or victims of corruption.
Subject to enhanced government reporting on net worth, corruption indices, and business affiliations, as well as investigations and asset tracing by the newly established Iran Kleptocracy Initiative.
affected_groups.group: Senior Iranian political figures, oligarchs, and parastatal entities

affected_groups.effect: Subject to potential review for sanctions following formal requests from congressional committee leaders to the President.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons supporting Iranian human rights abuses or censorship

key_provisions: Requires updates to federal internet freedom strategies regarding direct-to-cell wireless communications, drone-based platforms, signal jamming, and telecommunications providers in Iran, alongside extending the Iran Internet Freedom Grant Program with $30,000,000 authorized for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030.

Directs the Defense Innovation Unit to support the development of low-cost, scalable, and rapidly deployable technologies (such as low-Earth orbit satellite internet and mesh networking) to counter internet shutdowns in Iran, authorizing $2,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with other officials, to submit a detailed report identifying significant Iranian senior foreign political figures, oligarchs, parastatal entities, their economic exposures, and the effects of potential debt and equity restrictions.

Establishes an Iran Kleptocracy Initiative within the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to investigate, expose, disrupt, and prosecute corruption, money laundering, and racketeering by Iranian officials, proxies, and their families.

Requires the President to make determinations and submit written justifications regarding sanctions within 120 days of receiving a written request from congressional committee leaders concerning foreign persons who provide material support for human rights abuses, censorship, or repression in Iran.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Iran Human Rights, Internet Freedom, and Accountability Act of 2026 establishes policies and programs to support human rights, expand unrestricted internet access, and hold the regime of the Islamic Republic of Iran accountable for internal repression and corruption. The bill requires federal updates on internet freedom strategies, extends authorizations for internet freedom grants, directs the Defense Innovation Unit to develop anti-censorship technologies, mandates reports on Iranian political figures and parastatal entities, establishes an Iran Kleptocracy Initiative within FinCEN to target illicit assets, creates a congressional nomination process for human rights sanctions, and outlines a sense of Congress regarding broadcasting and support for independent journalists.
summary_detail.significance: This bill directs federal agencies to actively develop anti-censorship technology, track and investigate the financial assets of Iranian leadership, and enforce sanctions. It involves multiple federal bodies—including the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, the Defense Innovation Unit, and FinCEN—in executing foreign policy and financial enforcement regarding Iran.
